drivingQuestion: Why must the mishna state that the New Moon belongs to the coming month?
outcomeNote: answer continues in the next unit (מהו דתימא)

segments.he: ״חֹדֶשׁ זֶה״ — אָסוּר בְּכׇל הַחֹדֶשׁ, וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ לְהַבָּא. פְּשִׁיטָא! כִּי אִיצְטְרִיכָא לְחֹדֶשׁ חָסֵר,
segments.en: The mishna stated: If one says: «This month,» it is «forbidden» to him «for the entire» remainder of the «month, and» the «New Moon» is considered part «of the next» month. The Gemara asks: «Isn’t» this «obvious?» The Gemara answers: «When it was necessary» to teach this halakha it was «for» a New Moon preceding «a deficient,» twenty-nine-day «month.» In such a case the New Moon is celebrated for two days, the first of which is the thirtieth day of the previous month and the second of which is the first day of the new month. The case here is one where he took the vow on the first day of the New Moon.
